overview.oneLineTake: Nvidia's leadership shock and a 10-year yield back above 5% put equity volatility in expansion, so keep short-premium exposure defined and sized for gap risk.
themes: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned and the stock closed down over 4%. Indexes ended lower, QQQ -0.32% and SPY -0.35% on the day, with the turmoil framed as a threat to Wall Street's $500 billion AI financing bet.

Rates are the bigger fear. The 10-year yield jumped back above 5% as oil rose and traders price more Fed hikes. MarketWatch called it the biggest yield surge since 2022. Goolsbee called the inflation report "borderline disturbing."
Oil is firming after Trump said no Iran deal is needed, which feeds yields and inflation expectations.
AI dispersion is wide. Cerebras jumped 17% on revenue and a Microsoft deal, AMD rose 5.9% on a $700 target, and Cisco beat. Nebius fell about 17% on a weak outlook and higher capex.
Housing is weak, with existing-home sales at a 16-year low, and mortgage rates are rising again.
risks: Nvidia leadership vacuum and a pending investigation could spread to the wider AI complex and chip export policy ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.
A 10-year above 5% pressures long-duration equities and raises the odds of a rates-led selloff.
Oil and Strait of Hormuz headlines could add an inflation shock on top of hawkish Fed expectations.
Anthropic IPO supply and AI funding strain, including SoftBank warnings, could drain liquidity.

intelligence.headline: Nvidia Punches a Hole in Bull Case for AI Stocks
intelligence.summary: Nvidia and the fate of Jensen Huang is all that matters in markets this morning, because a big chunk of the AI trade that has propelled equity markets over the past four years depends on the company's chips. Huang is the co-founder, and under his watch the stock has returned 38% a year since its 1999 IPO, with gains even more stunning since OpenAI kicked off the AI boom in 2022. Joe Gilbert of Integrity Asset Management said he is "not only the face of AI but arguably the architect of the AI infrastructure" and that "it will be difficult if not impossible to replicate Jensen's vision." intelligence.headline: Alleged Spy at Center of Nvidia Scandal Has Returned to China
intelligence.summary: Alice Huang, the suspected spy at the center of the scandal, has returned to China, people familiar with the matter said. The allegations are adding to the strains between the US and China, days before Donald Trump travels to Shenzhen for a summit with Xi Jinping.

intelligence.headline: Chinese AI Stocks Tumble on Chip Access Fears
intelligence.summary: Chinese AI stocks are tumbling on concern that access to advanced chips may be curtailed. Alibaba ADRs are down 4.9% while model developers Z.AI and MiniMax sank 9.1% and 7.8%, respectively, in Hong Kong.

intelligence.headline: On the Move: Dell, Super Micro, CoreWeave, Eli Lilly
intelligence.summary: AI-related stocks sliding in premarket trading include Dell Technologies and Super Micro Computer, down more than 4% each. CoreWeave, which counts Nvidia as a key supplier and investor, is down 4.6%. Eli Lilly gains 3.7% after it won approval in China for a weight-loss tablet. Applied Materials and Nebius Group report before the opening bell. Cisco Systems and Cerebras Systems are up after the close.

intelligence.headline: Analysts Turn Less Bullish on Nvidia as Huang's Future Is Weighed
intelligence.summary: At the end of last week, 79 of 82 analysts tracked by Bloomberg had buys on Nvidia, a stock that has returned 760,000% since its IPO. Cracks were emerging in that consensus even before the New York Times reported yesterday that Huang had a second extramarital affair, this time with a subordinate. Analysts at Bernstein and Oppenheimer have cut their ratings this week, while Morgan Stanley removed the stock as a top pick. Baird cut its price target to $200 from $500. Dan Ives at Yorkville Ives put the estimated fair value of Nvidia without Huang at $225, versus $300 per share if he stays as C...

intelligence.headline: Anthropic IPO Is the Jenga Block Holding Up the AI Trade
intelligence.summary: Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs, said: "The Jenga block holding up the AI trade is the Anthropic IPO. So long as that comes out well, the whole sector will catch a bid. If Anthropic's IPO is massively overbought, AI stocks will rip." The drama around Huang at Nvidia has only added to the importance of Anthropic's IPO for the market's direction.

intelligence.headline: Gold Falls for a Third Day, Back Below $4,000 an Ounce
intelligence.summary: Gold is falling for a third day, extending a drop back below $4,000 an ounce as persistent US inflation and hawkish remarks from Fed officials fueled expectations for an interest-rate hike next month. Higher borrowing costs are typically a drag on gold as it doesn't pay interest.
